sourceSentences.text: # Proposed Workflow
Goal: `client brief + site + planning constraints -> floor-plan variants -> IFC/BIM -> validation -> attractive renders -> human review -> Archicad`.
## MoltNet tasks
- `extract-project-requirements`: derive storeys, rooms, target areas, garage, openings, orientation/style preferences and client priorities from source documents.
- `extract-planning-constraints`: derive setbacks, height, site coverage, roof, access, parking and other rules with source provenance.
Require human confirmation initially.
- `derive-building-program`: create the space programme, target/minimum areas, adjacency graph, circulation and orientation preferences.
- `solve-floor-plan`: use optimisation/constraint solving rather than LLM-generated arbitrary coordinates.
- `validate-plan`: check areas, widths, overlaps, topology, circulation, site boundary, setbacks, footprint, orientation and openings.
- `derive-building-elements`: create walls, slabs, roof, openings, doors/windows and other BIM elements.
- `export-or-update-ifc`: prefer mutating canonical IFC state where practical rather than maintaining a parallel full building model.
- `validate-ifc`: re-open the IFC and run semantic, IDS and geometric validation.
- `stage-visualisation`: add non-authoritative presentation assets such as materials, furniture, kitchen, vegetation and lighting.
- `render`: generate street, garden, interior, axonometric and plan views.
- `human-review`: let the designer/commercial user select or reject variants and iterate.
## POC phases
### POC 0 — Reconstruction
Reconstruct one supplied real project into IFC and verify that it can be inspected, rendered and eventually opened by the drafting team.
### POC 1 — Parametric modification
Change an extracted model (for example a larger living room, wider garage, added room) and solve a new valid configuration.
### POC 2 — Generation
Generate multiple layouts from brief + site + constraints, validate/rank them, then emit IFC + renders.
## Initial benchmark caveat
The handwritten starting brief and supplied plan are different design revisions.
The plan reflects later client modifications, so differences between them must not automatically be scored as generation errors.

# Proposed Workflow

Goal: `client brief + site + planning constraints -> floor-plan variants -> IFC/BIM -> validation -> attractive renders -> human review -> Archicad`.

## MoltNet tasks

- `extract-project-requirements`: derive storeys, rooms, target areas, garage, openings, orientation/style preferences and client priorities from source documents.
- `extract-planning-constraints`: derive setbacks, height, site coverage, roof, access, parking and other rules with source provenance. Require human confirmation initially.
- `derive-building-program`: create the space programme, target/minimum areas, adjacency graph, circulation and orientation preferences.
- `solve-floor-plan`: use optimisation/constraint solving rather than LLM-generated arbitrary coordinates.
- `validate-plan`: check areas, widths, overlaps, topology, circulation, site boundary, setbacks, footprint, orientation and openings.
- `derive-building-elements`: create walls, slabs, roof, openings, doors/windows and other BIM elements.
- `export-or-update-ifc`: prefer mutating canonical IFC state where practical rather than maintaining a parallel full building model.
- `validate-ifc`: re-open the IFC and run semantic, IDS and geometric validation.
- `stage-visualisation`: add non-authoritative presentation assets such as materials, furniture, kitchen, vegetation and lighting.
- `render`: generate street, garden, interior, axonometric and plan views.
- `human-review`: let the designer/commercial user select or reject variants and iterate.

## POC phases

### POC 0 — Reconstruction
Reconstruct one supplied real project into IFC and verify that it can be inspected, rendered and eventually opened by the drafting team.

### POC 1 — Parametric modification
Change an extracted model (for example a larger living room, wider garage, added room) and solve a new valid configuration.

### POC 2 — Generation
Generate multiple layouts from brief + site + constraints, validate/rank them, then emit IFC + renders.

## Initial benchmark caveat

The handwritten starting brief and supplied plan are different design revisions. The plan reflects later client modifications, so differences between them must not automatically be scored as generation errors.
input.problemDescription: One synthetic project, house-1, has a client brief, site information and planning constraints available. No building programme, floor-plan variant, IFC model, validation result or rendered view has been produced yet. A designer is available to review the result. Goal: house-1 has a reviewed design ready for the Archicad handoff described in the process.

stages.brief:
Stage 1 of a planning-domain design: extract the object types.

A type is a kind of thing an action takes as a parameter: agents, work items, places, resources. Include a kind of thing a step produces (for example a shipping label) only when later steps must refer to individual ones. Use a parent type when several kinds share behavior.

Modeling rules (classical PDDL with typing and negative preconditions):

- Names are lowercase and hyphenated: `parcel-label`, `truck-free`. Parameters start with `?`: `?t`, `?p`.

- Do not define the root type `object`; omit `parent` for top-level types.

- Actions cannot create objects. Every object an action uses must already exist in the problem. To model something a step produces (a receipt, a parcel label), use a pool of objects and a fact such as `(unused ?x)` that the producing action requires and deletes.

- For every action, list what must stop being true (delete effects), not only what becomes true. A fact nobody deletes stays true forever and can be reused by later steps.

- No quantifiers, conditional effects, or numeric fluents. Express "only one at a time" with a fact such as `(idle ?t)` that the action requires and deletes.

The example below only shows the JSON shape, using an unrelated library domain; do not reuse its names. Put in result {"types":[{"name":"person","description":"..."},{"name":"member","parent":"person","description":"..."},{"name":"book","description":"..."}]}.

Example: reading: {true: "{?b} is on the shelf", false: "{?b} is not on the shelf"}. Use simple words; do not add source requirements or action effects to these definitions.

- For every action, list what must stop being true (delete effects), not only what becomes true. A fact nobody deletes stays true forever and can be reused by later steps.

- No quantifiers, conditional effects, or numeric fluents. Express "only one at a time" with a fact such as `(idle ?t)` that the action requires and deletes.

stages.brief:
Supply reading as a neutral sentence describing the action, with every action parameter in braces, e.g. "{?m} borrows {?b}". Give action parameters distinct, readable label values such as "the member" and "the book". The sentence describes what happens, not whether the action or its rules are correct. Code will build prerequisite/effect claims from the formal arrays; do not write those claims yourself.

Stage 3: extract the actions. Each action has typed parameters, preconditions (literals; `negated: true` means the fact must be false), add effects, and delete effects, using only these predicates with their exact arity. `source` quotes the sentence the action models.

Modeling rules (classical PDDL with typing and negative preconditions):

- Names are lowercase and hyphenated: `parcel-label`, `truck-free`. Parameters start with `?`: `?t`, `?p`.

- Do not define the root type `object`; omit `parent` for top-level types.

- Actions cannot create objects. Every object an action uses must already exist in the problem. To model something a step produces (a receipt, a parcel label), use a pool of objects and a fact such as `(unused ?x)` that the producing action requires and deletes.

- For every action, list what must stop being true (delete effects), not only what becomes true. A fact nobody deletes stays true forever and can be reused by later steps.

- No quantifiers, conditional effects, or numeric fluents. Express "only one at a time" with a fact such as `(idle ?t)` that the action requires and deletes.

21: ### POC 2 — Generation
22: Generate multiple layouts from brief + site + constraints, validate/rank them, then emit IFC + renders.

1: # Proposed Workflow
2: Goal: `client brief + site + planning constraints -> floor-plan variants -> IFC/BIM -> validation -> attractive renders -> human review -> Archicad`.
3: ## MoltNet tasks
4: - `extract-project-requirements`: derive storeys, rooms, target areas, garage, openings, orientation/style preferences and client priorities from source documents.
5: - `extract-planning-constraints`: derive setbacks, height, site coverage, roof, access, parking and other rules with source provenance.
6: Require human confirmation initially.
7: - `derive-building-program`: create the space programme, target/minimum areas, adjacency graph, circulation and orientation preferences.
8: - `solve-floor-plan`: use optimisation/constraint solving rather than LLM-generated arbitrary coordinates.
9: - `validate-plan`: check areas, widths, overlaps, topology, circulation, site boundary, setbacks, footprint, orientation and openings.
10: - `derive-building-elements`: create walls, slabs, roof, openings, doors/windows and other BIM elements.
11: - `export-or-update-ifc`: prefer mutating canonical IFC state where practical rather than maintaining a parallel full building model.
12: - `validate-ifc`: re-open the IFC and run semantic, IDS and geometric validation.
13: - `stage-visualisation`: add non-authoritative presentation assets such as materials, furniture, kitchen, vegetation and lighting.
14: - `render`: generate street, garden, interior, axonometric and plan views.
15: - `human-review`: let the designer/commercial user select or reject variants and iterate.
16: ## POC phases
17: ### POC 0 — Reconstruction
18: Reconstruct one supplied real project into IFC and verify that it can be inspected, rendered and eventually opened by the drafting team.
19: ### POC 1 — Parametric modification
20: Change an extracted model (for example a larger living room, wider garage, added room) and solve a new valid configuration.
21: ### POC 2 — Generation
22: Generate multiple layouts from brief + site + constraints, validate/rank them, then emit IFC + renders.
23: ## Initial benchmark caveat
24: The handwritten starting brief and supplied plan are different design revisions.
25: The plan reflects later client modifications, so differences between them must not automatically be scored as generation errors.
</untrusted-numbered-description nonce="60d92a668eda">
